newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt lawyers to sue Netanyahu for pig posters.
newsitem.headline: Egypt lawyers to sue Netanyahu for pig posters.

text.p: Two Egyptian lawyers want to sue Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Cairo courts for more than $10 billion over posters plastered by an Israeli woman in the West Bank depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
Court sources on Monday said the lawyers held Netanyahu responsible for insults to their religious beliefs arising from the posters.

A Jewish woman, Tayana Suskin, 26, will stand trial for putting up the posters in the West Bank city of Hebron in June, igniting a wave of unrest in the volatile city where 400 Jews live among 100,000 Arabs.

Suskin is accused of committing a racist act, harming religious sensitivities, supporting a terrorist group and endangering life for stoning an Arab car. She could face a maximum jail sentence of 26 years if convicted.

Egyptian lawyer Mostafa Ashoub, a Moslem, took his case to court earlier this month to claim $10 billion in damages from Netanyahu for the poster incident which Ashoub said insulted his religious sensitivity, court sources said.
Ashoub told the court in his application for the civil case that if he won, the money should go to Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak for distribution in the name of propagation of religion.

"I raised this case against the Israeli prime minister because he is responsible for civil rights and he is the primary inciter of extremists in Israel to attack Arabs and their sacred things," Ashoub said. The court will pass verdict on August 31.

A second case, which will open on September 8, has been brought by Coptic Christian lawyer Mamdouh Nakhla, who plans to claim one million pounds ($295,000) from Netanyahu as compensation for what he has described as the psychological harm and insult incurred to his beliefs from the posters, the sources said.
